title: api: multipart file input support + per-file/request limits + content-type validation (openai-compat)
author: Samir Patel
description:
Motivation: Enable first-class multipart/form-data file inputs for tool/function-calling and OpenAI-compat endpoints while preventing memory/DoS issues by enforcing per-file and per-request limits and strict content-type validation. This PR implements a multipart parser that runs prior to streaming responses, enforces configurable file_size and total_payload limits, validates content-type against an allowlist (image/*, audio/*, text/*, application/pdf, application/json), and maps validation errors to OpenAI-compat error responses.

What this changes (summary):
- Add multipart parsing middleware for API endpoints that accept files (tools, file input in create-chat-completion-like endpoints). The parser extracts files and form fields, stores small files in-memory and streams large files to a temp store within configured thresholds.
- Enforce configurable limits: per_file_size_limit (default 10MB), total_request_payload_limit (default 50MB), max_files_per_request (default 5). Limits configurable via config/defaults.yaml and per-customer overrides for Dedicated/Private.
- Strict Content-Type validation with mappings to OpenAI-compat error codes to match client expectations. Unknown/unsupported content-types produce a 415 with a JSON error body compatible with OpenAI error schema.
- Streaming stability changes: the multipart parser completes header/form parsing and basic validation before the generation stream is established to avoid interleaving file ingestion with token streaming. For files larger than streaming threshold we fallback to buffered temp storage with backpressure to avoid unbounded memory growth.
- Add feature-flag (api.experimental.multipart_streaming) to enable incremental rollout; default off for older tenants to avoid behavioral changes.
- Docs updates to openai-compat.md and SDK compatibility shim in python SDK to illustrate multipart usage.

Checklist: 
- [x] Middleware + parser implementation
- [x] Limits and config entries + unit tests
- [x] Content-Type allowlist and OpenAI-compatible error mapping
- [x] Streaming integration and fallback behavior tests
- [x] Integration tests for common client scenarios (curl/form-data, SDKs)
- [x] Docs and changelog entry

Compatibility notes:
- Behaviour is guarded by a feature flag and opt-in on existing tenants. New tenants will see multipart enabled by default. The compatibility shim mirrors OpenAI semantics for error payloads and status codes to minimize client-side changes. Developers using streaming + files should be aware streaming will not start until initial multipart parsing is complete; this prevents partial stream races we observed in perf canary tests.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests added for parser edge cases (malformed boundaries, missing content-type, file count limits).
- Integration tests for standard clients: curl --form, python requests, TS fetch with FormData.
- Added a perf canary that uploaded mixed small/large files and validated memory under load.
- Ran canary on staging with 1K parallel small-file requests to verify limits and backpressure behavior.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag gated rollout starting with internal tenants, then enable by default for new tenants after 2 weeks of canary monitoring.
- Monitor metrics: multipart.parse_errors, multipart.backpressure_events, api.file_rejected_limit, streaming.init_latency.

Notes on design decisions:
- We parse the multipart envelope fully enough to validate headers and file sizes before establishing the token streaming connection. This trades a small additional latency for deterministic behavior and far fewer streaming race conditions.
- Files above the in-memory threshold are spooled to ephemeral temp storage that respects tenant storage limits. This avoids OOMs observed in the incident logs that motivated this change.

References: Linear ENG-1453 (API multipart), SUP-324 (support ticket where a customer hit unbounded RAM usage with streaming uploads), design doc link: internal.redwood/designs/api-multipart (private).

review_thread: Aditi Rao: The parser looks good, but I'm concerned about the synchronous parse before streaming — can this add significant latency for large requests?

Samir Patel: We considered that; the parser only validates headers and size prefixes up to the in-memory threshold. Large files are spooled to disk incrementally while validation guarantees do not wait for full upload. The added latency for small files is negligible (sub-10ms) in our canary runs.
Marcus Lee: Please add metrics for backpressure events and ensure we expose tenant-config overrides. Also suggest a unit test for malformed boundary behavior.
Samir Patel: Added multipart.backpressure_events metric and tenant override config in defaults.yaml. Added unit test for malformed boundary (tests/unit/test_multipart_limits.py).
Helen Zhang: Lint failure in openai_compat.py and a flaky test observed on first CI run. Can you address?
Samir Patel: Fixed linter formatting and extended the integration test timeout; CI rerun passed.
Aditi Rao: Approving — validated canary results and memory profiles.
Marcus Lee: Approving — tests and metrics look good.

New configurable limits: per_file_size_limit (default 10MB), total_request_payload_limit (default 50MB), max_files_per_request (default 5). Content-Type allowlist enforcement and OpenAI-compatible error responses. Feature-flag gated rollout.
